title: model loading breadcrumbs - weights/shard failures (scratchpad)
content:
Scratchpad / breadcrumbs for the model loading incidents we've been seeing (weights download + shard issues). Mostly notes to self while reproducing and triaging.

Symptoms observed:
- Intermittent failures when loading ResNet-like model (large LLM variant) from s3-backed model store. Failures occur ~5-10% of attempts across routes.
- Error variants seen:
  * IOError / OSError during torch.load: "EOFError: Ran out of input" or "unexpected end of file"
  * Checksum mismatch: "Expected sha256=abcd... but got 1234..." reported by post-download verify step
  * Missing shard file: "model-00003-of-00010.pt not found" even though list-objects shows it present earlier
  * safetensors loader: "IndexError: offset out of bounds" when trying to load corrupted .safetensors
  * Runtime error: "Storages' sizes don't match" on state_dict load (sizes differ between shards)
  * Transient EPIPE / connection reset by peer from S3 during download

Commands / troubleshooting steps tried (chronological):
1) Reproduce locally (on dev VM):
   - aws s3 cp s3://rw-model-store/models/my-llm/v3/model-00003-of-00010.pt ./ --quiet --no-progress --only-show-errors
   - Result: sometimes exits with code 0 but smaller file size (partial).
   - Follow-up: aws s3api head-object --bucket rw-model-store --key models/my-llm/v3/model-00003-of-00010.pt -> reports ContentLength=504857600
   - md5sum / sha256sum locally: computed sha256 doesn't match manifest.

2) Retry/resume attempts:
   - curl -C - -o model-00003-of-00010.pt "<presigned-url>" --retry 8 --retry-delay 2 --retry-max-time 120
   - aria2c -x 16 -s 16 "<presigned-url>" (parallel segmented download) -> produced consistent file sometimes, but occasionally still corrupted.

3) Cross-check via alternate clients / regions:
   - gsutil cp (when mirrored to GCS) -> similar partial/EOF errors seen (suggests not just AWS SDK bug).
   - azcopy test -> similar behavior.

4) Inspect storage/network layer on node:
   - df -h -> disk had <10% free at time of some failures. OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device seen in one run.
   - dmesg -> NIC reported some link flaps around same window (not consistent).

5) Verify manifest and shard list logic:
   - cat manifest.json -> lists 10 shards with sizes and sha256 checksums.
   - Quick script to iterate over shards: for i in shards: head-object -> compare ContentLength vs manifest size; if mismatch, record. Found small number of shards where head-object size != manifest size (N=2).

6) Attempt to load in alternative format:
   - Tried safetensors loader (faster validation) -> immediate IndexError for one shard -> indicates file corruption, not loader bug.

7) Run local join + torch.load test:
   - python -c "import torch; sd=torch.load('model-00001-of-00010.pt', map_location='cpu')" -> for corrupted shards this fails with EOFError or Storage mismatch.

Hypotheses / possible root causes:
- Partial download due to flaky network + no atomic rename or temp-file verify step in model puller (download finishes but is truncated/overwritten).
- Storage side corruption (S3 replication/inconsistency) — although S3 guarantees should rule this out, we do see mismatch between head-object sizes and manifest for some objects. Could be inconsistent upload earlier.
- On-node disk pressure causing writer to truncate or fail during streaming write (Errno 28 observed).
- Old model-puller code path uses streaming + direct write to target path (not writing to .tmp and rename), exposing consumers to partial files.
- Checksum verification is running but only post-load; we need pre-load validation and atomic replace.
- Mismatch between checkpoint format used when saving vs loader expected (hf vs safetensors vs torch) — possible if a quantized variant was saved but the loading path expects full float.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Added quick pre-download verify step in local tests: download to tmp file + compute sha256 -> only rename into model directory if match. This eliminated local partial-load repro on my machine.
- For live service, increasing disk pressure alert thresholds and freeing local cache (temp model dir purge) reduced occurrences for a short window.
- Instrumented download code with Content-Length vs manifest length check and simple retry loop (3 attempts with exponential backoff).

Evidence / logs (snippets):
- Example error from runtime logs:
  2024-11-14T18:24:02Z ERROR runtime.model-loader [req=abcd1234] Failed to load shard model-00003-of-00010.pt: EOFError: Ran out of input
  2024-11-14T18:24:02Z WARN runtime.model-loader [req=abcd1234] shard-size(expected=504857600) != downloaded-size(23456712)
- Example aws error seen intermittently:
  botocore.exceptions.ProtocolError: ('Connection broken: IncompleteRead(8192 bytes read)', IncompleteRead(8192))

Next steps / TODOs (ordered):
- [ ] Open storage ticket to run integrity scan on s3 prefix models/my-llm/v3 (JIRA-MLINF-1223 created) -> ask for full object checksums and replication status. (assigned to storage: @Jordan Wu)
- [ ] Add atomic download pattern in model-puller: download -> verify checksum -> atomic rename. Patch in runtime repo and test. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/2041 (WIP).
- [ ] Add preflight head-object size check and manifest mismatch alert (early-fail).
- [ ] Add disk-pressure gating in model-puller: if free space < threshold, fail fast and escalate to SRE rather than attempt partial writes.
- [ ] Add alerting/metric: model_download_partial_count, model_download_checksum_mismatch_count.
- [ ] Re-run load tests with parallel clients (50 concurrent) after patch to ensure no regressions.
- [ ] Investigate possible uploader bug that created corrupted objects (check upstream export pipeline).

Notes / lessons:
- Writing downloads directly to final path is dangerous when consumers try to open immediately. Always write to temporary path + atomic rename.
- Checksum verification should be done before exposing artifact to loaders; loaders should also validate quickly and fail with clear telemetry.
- If disk pressure is common on inference nodes, put model cache on a separate mount with quota/eviction policy.

Quick reproduction recipe (dev):
1) Simulate partial download: use dd to truncate file after download start:
   dd if=model-00003-of-00010.pt of=model-00003-of-00010.pt.part bs=1 count=$((filesize/4))
2) Run python load -> observe EOFError / Storage size mismatch.
3) Test patched puller that writes to .part then verifies sha256; should reject truncated file.

Questions I still have / open items:
- Are uploads done with single PUT or multipart? Multipart uploads risk leaving incomplete parts if aborted; need to confirm uploader behavior.
- Any recent infra changes around NFS mounts or node-local caching that coincide with timeline? (ask SRE).
- Should we switch to safetensors by default for large checkpoints to get faster validation? Pros/cons to discuss.

If anyone else picking this up: start with model manifest and storage audit (head-object vs manifest); then push the atomic-download + verify patch to a canary fleet and validate. Logs to look for: "shard-size(expected", "downloaded-size", "EOFError: Ran out of input".

End of scratchpad.
